title: Remove dead auth-session/throttle production gates; fix post-auth-removal docs
opportunity: A prior uncommitted change removed the username/password login system (AuthEndpoints/AuthStore/AuthThrottle/DistributedAuthThrottle/PasswordHasher), but ProductionReadinessPolicy and ProductionHealth still validated Auth:SessionIdleMinutes/Auth:SessionAbsoluteHours/Auth:MaxFailedAttempts/Auth:LockoutMinutes/Auth:Throttle:* and probed for the deleted waf_auth_throttle_buckets table. A Production deployment following docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md would be required to configure a login-abuse subsystem that no longer exists, and the health check could report a false 'migration not installed' failure. README.md, docs/SECURITY.md and docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md still described the removed login system as current behavior (first-run wizard admin step, bootstrap admin password, roles/permission matrix, session cookies).
implementation: Remove the Auth:SessionIdleMinutes/Auth:SessionAbsoluteHours/Auth:MaxFailedAttempts/Auth:LockoutMinutes and Auth:Throttle:* checks from ProductionReadinessPolicy.Validate.
Remove the waf_auth_throttle_buckets table probe from PostgresHealthCheck in ProductionHealth.cs.
Remove the now-unused Auth:Throttle config section from appsettings.json.
Drop the two ProductionReadinessPolicyTests asserting the removed bounds checks.

Rewrite README.md (first-run wizard, access model, configuration table, breaking changes) and correct docs/SECURITY.md and docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md to describe the current network-perimeter AdminGuard model instead of the removed login system.
Soften the Desktop Audit nav hint text, which promised 'who logged in' with no login identity to record.

tests.red: N/A (dead-code/doc correction, not new behavior; verified by inspection and full regression)
tests.manifest: 6 files; hash and length verification passed

boundaries: Live Browser/EXE smoke, external penetration/load/SLO/SIEM/CodeQL validation, and Authenticode signing were not performed.

Database migrations 006_auth_rbac.sql and 009_distributed_security_limits.sql still create the now-unused users/waf_auth_throttle_buckets tables; migration files are append-only/checksum-verified and were intentionally left untouched in this module.
